title: Canary-less Event Fanout / Global Outage on Poison Pill
pattern: An event or operation dispatcher that concurrently pushes a newly modified, risky, or heavy command payload (such as schema updates, complex migrations, or heavy parsing requests) to all production server nodes in parallel without a sequential testing gate.
why_bad: If the payload contains a code bug, unexpected edge case, or heavy memory load, dispatching it globally will trigger concurrent crashes or memory exhaustion across all server nodes simultaneously [159]. This causes an instant, complete global outage [159]. Resilient systems must employ a sequential "canary" request first to verify host stability before broad deployment [159].
detection: A concurrency mapping function fanning out untested operations across a production collection without a sequential canary execution step.
fix: Enforce a sequential canary gate: dispatch the operation to a single node first, wait for a success response, and only proceed to scale out globally upon verification [159].
source: Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 6 / passage [159].
